## 14. T045-b1 — the acquire→run grind on the shipped one-command path

Worker unit `bank-demo-fleet-pipeline-p2f/T045-b1-acquire-run-grind`. 2026-08-20, at `d31a906`.
First unit of board task T045. Everything below went through the **shipped** path only:
`acquire` for the network half (`VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE=consented`, consent
`VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10`), then the single `intervention-count` → `run` command with all
five install policies declared and `VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE` unset. No `--revision` was
hand-carried anywhere: T043-a's finding held, and the journalled revision was adopted through
the four ingest gates by itself. No source under `packages/**` was changed.

The declaration used for every run in this unit, verbatim:

```
node --experimental-strip-types packages/cli/src/cli.ts intervention-count <baseline> \
  --out <lane> --record evidence/runs/<id>/run-record.json --json \
  --allow-remote-tarballs --allow-install-scripts --allow-peer-conflicts \
  --allow-foreign-lockfile --allow-git-dependencies
```

Five policies, one command, nothing opted into per application.

### 14.1 Enumeration (recorded before any run)

**Coverage before this unit** (`evidence/trust/current/coverage-report.json` totals):
`{applications: 23, proven: 11, bounded: 2, refused: 5, not-admitted: 5}`. Census 198 sites,
`matchesPublished` true. Freeze composite `140ce86e…`. Matrix `react: 6 counted of 6`,
`angular: 4 counted of 4`.

**Priority 1 — the five staged react apps T043-a enumerated as gate-blocked.** Their source
identity was read off the old-goal journals under `evidence/ingests/<app>/<t-namespace>/`, and
the licence each carries at its pin was read off the staged tree on disk:

| Staged id | Repository @ pin (from the old journal) | Licence at pin | This unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `react-verdaccio-stage-t682` | `verdaccio/verdaccio` @ `4fd08e63…` (v4.12.2) | **MIT** (`package.json` `license: MIT`, root `LICENSE` "MIT License") | **acquired + run** — §14.2 |
| `react-jaeger-ui-stage-t680` | `jaegertracing/jaeger-ui` @ `1ceadb6f…` | **Apache-2.0** | **not acquired** — §14.5 |
| `react-saleor-dashboard-t670-stage` | `saleor/saleor-dashboard` @ `04354fa3…` (2.11.1) | **BSD-3-Clause** | **not acquired** — §14.5 |
| `react-appsmith-stage-t685` | `appsmithorg/appsmith` @ `16c509d9…` (v1.5.9) | **Apache-2.0** | **not acquired** — §14.5 |
| `react-strapi-stage-t687` | `strapi/strapi` @ `8972d78e…` (v3.6.8) | **`SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE`**; the root `LICENSE` opens "Portions of the Strapi software are licensed as follows" | **not acquired** — §14.5 |

**Priority 2 — the old six-app react batch's named-refusal apps.** Both already carry a
`versionless.official-source.v1` acquire record under `VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10` and both
baselines were already on disk, so neither was re-acquired: re-running `acquire` would have
**rewritten** an existing published `source.json`, and this unit appends rather than rewrites.
The run is the thing T045 is buying, and the run is what was spent.

- `react-coverview-a1470b01` — `rutikwankhade/CoverView` @ `a1470b01…`, MIT.
- `react-antd-admin-template-v2-0-0` — `NLRX-WJC/react-antd-admin-template` @ `31fc5dfa…` (v2.0.0), MIT.

**Priority 3 — one fresh Angular CLI-era candidate.** Not attempted this unit; §14.6.

### 14.2 `react-verdaccio-v4-12-2` — acquire **source-bound**, run **refused: `ingest.frontend-root-declares-no-framework`** (1 of 9 stages ran), interventionCount 0

The acquire went through cleanly and is the first thing in this repository to prove the
generic path end to end on a repository it had no module for:

```
VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE=consented node --experimental-strip-types packages/cli/src/cli.ts \
  acquire verdaccio/verdaccio --ref v4.12.2 --id react-verdaccio-v4-12-2 \
  --consent VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10 --json
```

`result: source-bound`, 7 requests, 3.1 s wall. `refs/tags/v4.12.2` resolved as an **annotated**
tag `48c9f8bc…` dated `2021-06-23T17:16:55Z` onto commit `4fd08e63557d6bfd0e1183b60e8bc4c3a9f14bff`
— **the same commit the T682 journal recorded**, so the pin the old goal fetched and the pin the
shipped path resolves are the same object. Archive parity: `missingFiles 0, extraFiles 0,
mismatchedBlobs 0` over 525 git blobs / 751 safe entries, single root
`verdaccio-4fd08e63557d6bfd0e1183b60e8bc4c3a9f14bff`. Licence read at the pin:
`identifier MIT`, `identifierSource observed`, `Copyright (c) 2018 Verdaccio community`.
Record at `evidence/ingests/react-verdaccio-v4-12-2/source.json`, attempt
`25537a2e…`, baseline at `.versionless/work/react-verdaccio-v4-12-2/baseline`.

The run then stopped at ingest, verbatim:

> Ingest: none of the directories considered declares react, next or angular, so this stage read
> no frontend to admit: `.` declares no framework this stage reads. A directory carrying a
> manifest is not a frontend; declare the one that is with `--frontend-root <dir>`.

**No `--frontend-root` was declared, because there is none to declare.** Verdaccio 4.12.2 does
not carry its React UI in this tree: the root manifest declares zero `react` dependency (only
`eslint-plugin-react` and `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` as devDependencies), and every other
`package.json` under the pin that mentions `react` is a fixture inside `test/` or
`docker-examples/`. The UI ships from a separate package at this era. The refusal is therefore
**terminal and correct**: the pipeline was pointed at a Node registry server and said so.

The analyze row that did run is still worth the ink: `packageManager {manager: yarn, lockfiles: [yarn.lock]}`,
`nodeEra {declared: "13", source: ".nvmrc"}`, and 112 dependencies all `unknown` to the cell —
"The frozen React and Next.js adapters publish no target-cell package registry, so no per-package
verdict exists for this lineage."

**Finding: `react-verdaccio` was mis-enumerated as a react candidate.** It is not one at this pin.
The T682 staging tree on disk has always been a Node server. That is not a pipeline wall — it is
the pipeline correctly declining to invent a frontend, at intervention count 0, in 0.3 s.

### 14.3 `react-coverview-a1470b01` — **PROVEN**, 9 of 9 stages ran, interventionCount 0

The one the packet said could reach proven today, and it did.

Prior record (T029 batch): `defect` at `install`, exit 1 — "the declared policies were applied and
the pinned closure still did not install", `npm install … --legacy-peer-deps` failing on a
git-protocol dependency the batch had no policy for. That record is preserved, renamed to
`evidence/runs/react-coverview-a1470b01/t029-install-defect-run-record.json` (+ `.interventions.json`)
per the u6 pattern; nothing was deleted or rewritten.

Re-run with `--allow-git-dependencies` declared alongside the other four:

- `outcome: proceeded`, `exitCode 0`
- `analyze:ran ingest:ran license-at-pin:ran era-cell:ran plan:ran apply:ran install:ran build:ran witness:ran`
- `interventionCount 0`, `invocations 1`, `stdinReads 0`, `mutatedPathsOutsideWriteSet []`, `authoringPathsTouched []`
- `terminalClassification: "proven"`
- roots: `frontendBasis: ". declares react ^16.14.0 (dependencies.react)"` — the application root is its own frontend root
- coverage row: `{status: "proven", provenanceOfStatus: "run-record", interventionCount: 0, source: {repository: "rutikwankhade/CoverView", ref/revision: "a1470b01e41c9e1128364e500b2ca2107f8432e0", license: "MIT"}}`

**T028 bar met exactly: 9/9 `ran` and count 0.** This is the second application ever admitted to
proven by run-record derivation, and the first one the `git-dependencies` policy bought.
`react-flame-v2-4-0` was the template; this is the template applied to an application the
policy work of T043-b was aimed at.

### 14.4 `react-antd-admin-template-v2-0-0` — **refused: `install.closure-registry-unreachable`** (6 of 9 stages ran), interventionCount 0

Prior record (T029 batch) was a **defect** at install, exit 1 — npm failed and the flow had no
name for why. Preserved as `t029-install-defect-run-record.json` (+ `.interventions.json`).

Re-run with the same five policies: `outcome: refused`, exit 2,
`analyze:ran ingest:ran license-at-pin:ran era-cell:ran plan:ran apply:ran install:refused
build:not-run witness:not-run`, `interventionCount 0`. The refusal, verbatim:

> Install: this closure pins `registry.npm.taobao.org`, and npm could not reach it —
> `CERT_HAS_EXPIRED`, requesting `https://registry.npm.taobao.org/word-wrap/download/word-wrap-1.2.3.tgz`.
> There is no policy to declare here and this flow offers none: no allowance makes an unreachable
> registry answer, and a closure that resolves through a registry that is gone cannot be installed
> as recorded. What this establishes is that this run did not reach `registry.npm.taobao.org`;
> whether that host is retired or momentarily unreachable is not established here, and neither is
> what it would have served. The remedy is re-pinning the closure onto a registry that answers,
> which changes what the application declares and is therefore a migration decision rather than an
> install policy.

**This is the honesty motion the packet predicted, measured.** The same application, the same
pinned closure, the same host: what was an unnamed `defect` is now a named `refused` with the
non-claim attached ("whether that host is retired … is not established here"). A defect says the
pipeline broke; a refusal says the world did. The second is true here, and the flow now says so.

### 14.5 Not attempted this unit — **consent scope**, and why that is the honest answer

Four of the five priority-1 staged apps were **not acquired**. The reason is not budget and not a
pipeline wall: it is that the charter's consent grant names one licence.

> "Use purpose-bound consent ID `VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10` for acquisition of public **MIT**
> source and dependencies." — `docs/goals/legacy-react-angular-production-readiness/goal.md`,
> restated in `docs/goals/next-tranche-strategy/goal.md` as "for any public MIT acquisition".

`jaeger-ui` and `appsmith` are Apache-2.0, `saleor-dashboard` is BSD-3-Clause, and `strapi` v3.6.8
declares `SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE` over a root `LICENSE` that opens "Portions of the Strapi software
are licensed as follows" — a split-terms file, the least clear of the four. None is MIT.

Two facts point in opposite directions and both are recorded rather than resolved here:

1. **Against the strict reading:** `react-your-spotify-1-5-0` is already in this corpus, acquired
   under `VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10`, with `licence.identifier: "GPL-3.0"` — so a non-MIT source
   has been fetched under this grant before, and `acquire.ts` itself applies no SPDX filter (its
   licence gate is a presence-and-identification check, per its own header).
2. **For the strict reading:** every one of these four was originally acquired under its **own**
   purpose-bound consent — `T680-jaeger-ui-production-acquisition`,
   `T670-saleor-dashboard-production-acquisition`, `T685-appsmith-v1.5.9-production-acquisition`,
   `T687-strapi-v3.6.8-production-acquisition`. The previous goal minted a separate grant per
   non-MIT application, which is exactly what one does when the corpus grant does not reach.

The standing rule is "do NOT acquire on an uncertain consent", and fact 2 is a strong signal that
the corpus grant was never meant to reach these. So: **no socket was opened for any of the four.**
They are recorded as `not-attempted-this-unit: consent-scope-unresolved`, and the question is
escalated to the owner rather than decided by a worker. This costs four candidates and buys the

## 15. T045-b3 — the two zero-cost RUNNABLE-NOW candidates, run

Worker unit `bank-demo-fleet-pipeline-p2f/T045-b3-zero-cost-pair`. 2026-08-20. Both applications
were already in the corpus with baselines on disk, so **no socket was opened for acquisition, no
consent question was raised, and no `--frontend-root` or `--cell` was declared.** Both carried a
published `refused: install.lockfile-foreign` row recorded 2026-08-17 — three days before
`--allow-foreign-lockfile` shipped in T043-b. This unit is what that policy is worth on them.

Identical declaration to §14, verbatim, once per application, `VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE` unset:

```
node --experimental-strip-types packages/cli/src/cli.ts intervention-count <baseline> \
  --out <fresh lane> --record evidence/runs/<id>/run-record.json --json \
  --allow-remote-tarballs --allow-install-scripts --allow-peer-conflicts \
  --allow-foreign-lockfile --allow-git-dependencies
```

Prior records preserved under the u6/b1 pattern, nothing deleted or rewritten:
`evidence/runs/<id>/t030-lockfile-foreign-run-record.json` (+ `.interventions.json`) for both.

### 15.1 `react-cra-redux-1a06509b` — **PROVEN**, 9 of 9 stages ran, interventionCount 0

`notrab/create-react-app-redux` @ `1a06509b0c0e5a3440f8c1e1d1cc7b8169d7988f`, MIT
(`identifierSource: observed`, "verbatim MIT text in the repository root LICENSE file at the
pinned revision", `Copyright (c) 2017 Jamie Barton`). 440 K, 12 declared dependencies.

| stage | status | ms | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| analyze | ran | 1 | `yarn` / `yarn.lock`; 12 deps, all `unknown` to the cell |
| ingest | ran | 4 | `frontendSource: read`, `. declares react 16.14.0 (dependencies.react)` |
| license-at-pin | ran | 0 | MIT, observed |
| era-cell | ran | 15 | `already-present`, cell `react-vite-lane`, runtime **v24.15.0** — era `not-read`: all seven era sources absent |
| plan | ran | 0 | `@versionless/react craEntryDocument (create-react-app adapter)` |
| apply | ran | 7 | `materialized`, 21 files copied, `index.html` derived from `public/index.html`, entry `/src/index.js` |
| install | ran | 12 423 | npm, `foreignLockfileDisregarded` — `yarn.lock` left untouched and **not consulted** |
| build | ran | 976 | Vite 8.0.16 lane |
| witness | ran | 2 681 | synthesized crawl, 1 journey, `replayabilityRatio 1`, 1 of 4 declared routes reached, `mode: offline`, `successfulNonLoopback 0` |

`outcome: proceeded`, `exitCode 0`, `interventionCount 0`, `invocations 1`, `stdinReads 0`,
`mutatedPathsOutsideWriteSet []`, `authoringPathsTouched []`, `terminalClassification: "proven"`.
**T028 bar met exactly: 9/9 `ran` and count 0.** Coverage row moves `refused` → **`proven`**,
`provenanceOfStatus: run-record`. The screen's prediction held to the letter: the wall it named
(install, answered by the policy) fell, and nothing between install and witness refused.

The bound on the proof is stated in the record and is worth carrying: the install
**disregarded** the era lockfile. Verbatim, from the install row —

> "npm resolved every dependency fresh from the lane manifest instead. This resolution is NOT
> pinned by the era lockfile, so the installed closure may drift from the one the era application
> shipped with, and every claim downstream of this install is bounded by that drift."

That is the price of `--allow-foreign-lockfile` and it applies to coverview and flame too. Proven
here means *this* closure built and witnessed, not that the 2017 closure did.

### 15.2 `react-your-spotify-1-5-0` — **defect at `build`** (7 of 9 stages ran), interventionCount 0

`Yooooomi/your_spotify` @ its corpus pin, **GPL-3.0** (`identifierSource: observed`, "verbatim

| stage | status | ms | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| analyze | ran | 1 | `yarn` / `yarn.lock`; 38 deps, all `unknown` to the cell |
| ingest | ran | 31 | `frontendSource: **read**`, `frontend: …/baseline/client` |
| license-at-pin | ran | 1 | GPL-3.0, observed |
| era-cell | ran | 4 | `provisioned`, cell `node-16`, runtime **v16.20.2** |
| plan | ran | 1 | CRA adapter, `frameworkVersionDeclared ^18.2.0`, builder `react-scripts` |
| apply | ran | 73 | `materialized`, 330 files copied, entry `/src/index.tsx` |
| install | ran | 15 586 | npm, `yarn.lock` disregarded under policy |
| **build** | **defect** | 471 | see below |
| witness | not-run | 0 | — |

`outcome: defect`, `exitCode 1`, `interventionCount 0`, `terminalClassification: "defect:build"`.
Coverage row moves `refused` → **`not-admitted`**, `statusReason: "run-did-not-proceed:defect"` —
the same shape angular2-hn's build defect carries (§13).

**The frontend-root question the screen flagged: no divergence.** `frontendSource` is `read`, not
declared; basis verbatim: `client declares react ^18.2.0 (dependencies.react); server declares no
framework this stage reads`. The screen's reading of `ingest.ts:465-600` reproduced the shipped
behaviour exactly, and no declaration was improvised.

**The defect, by name.** The build row's reason, verbatim in its load-bearing part:

> `build: npm run build failed in the lane. This is a defect rather than a refusal: the lane was
> composed and installed and the build still did not complete. Command failed: npm run build`
> `You are using Node.js 16.20.2. Vite requires Node.js version 20.19+ or 22.12+. Please upgrade
> your Node.js version.`
> `ReferenceError: CustomEvent is not defined`
> `    at EventTarget.parse (…/lanes/your-spotify/node_modules/vite/dist/node/cli.js:533:28)`

with the runtime block naming its own provenance:

> `cellSupplier: "workspace-runtime-cache"`, `cellVersion: "v16.20.2"`,
> `pathPrefix: ".versionless/cache/angular-13-cell-runtime/node-v16.20.2-darwin-arm64"`

**This is a contradiction inside the shipped flow, not a property of the application.** The
era-cell stage read the *era* of the source tree — `client/Dockerfile` line 1 is `FROM
node:16-alpine`, confirmed on disk, and the stage recorded `readFrom: "Dockerfile#FROM line 1"`,
`declared: "node:16-alpine"` — and provisioned Node 16.20.2. But the lane the plan and apply
stages composed is **not** the era lane: the frozen React adapter migrates CRA to Vite, and the
lane manifest that install resolved declares `vite 8.0.16` with `"build": "vite build"`. Vite 8
requires Node 20.19+/22.12+. So the era reading was applied to a migrated toolchain that the era
runtime cannot run.

`react-cra-redux` is the control, and it is a clean one: the *same* adapter, the *same* Vite
8.0.16, the *same* five policies — and it built, because its tree names no era at all (all seven
era sources absent, `era.outcome: not-read`), so era-cell fell through to `react-vite-lane` at the
host runtime v24.15.0. **The only difference between proven and defect across these two runs is
whether the source tree happened to contain a Dockerfile.** An application is penalised for
declaring its era more precisely than one that declares nothing.

Two further readings, recorded not decided:

- The runtime that was provisioned came out of `.versionless/cache/angular-13-cell-runtime/` — the
  Angular 13 cell's own runtime cache, borrowed for a React lineage run. Whether that borrow is
  intended is not established here.
- The competing repair shapes are (a) era-cell should read the era of the **composed lane**, not
  the source, for lineages whose adapter replaces the toolchain; or (b) the build stage should
  refuse by name (`build.era-runtime-cannot-run-migrated-toolchain`) rather than emit a defect,
  since nothing is broken — two correct readings simply disagree. Both are source changes under
  `packages/**` and out of this unit's contract. Filed, not attempted.

### 15.3 Coverage delta

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `applications` | 24 | 24 |
| `proven` | 12 | **13** |
| `bounded` | 2 | 2 |
| `refused` | 7 | **5** |
| `not-admitted` | 3 | **4** |

Reconciled row by row:

- `react-cra-redux-1a06509b`: `refused` → **`proven`** (+1 proven, −1 refused)
- `react-your-spotify-1-5-0`: `refused` → **`not-admitted`** (−1 refused, +1 not-admitted)

**Proven 12 → 13.** The floor the guards hold at 12 grew rather than moved. The second move is a
loss on the published surface and should be read as one: a named refusal became an unnamed defect,
which is the *reverse* of §14.9 finding 2's honesty motion. It is still forward progress on the
question T045 asks — the wall moved from `install` to `build`, three sessions of evidence deep —
but the row it leaves behind says less than the row it replaced, and §15.2's repair (b) is
precisely the motion that would give it a name back.

**Guards, all checked after publishing:**

- `react: 6 counted of 6 proven cells` — unchanged; a run-record proof is not a Judge-counted cell.
- `angular: 4 counted of 4 proven cells` — verbatim.
- `adapter-freeze.json` composite `140ce86e163d…` — unmoved; no source changed.
- `evidence/runs/react-flame-v2-4-0`, `react-coverview-a1470b01`, `angular2-hn` — byte-identical to `HEAD`.
- `git diff HEAD -- packages` — empty.

### 15.4 Publish state

Batch ordering, after the second record landed:

- `trust:generate --offline --policy trust/policy.json --output evidence/trust/current`
  (with `VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE=offline`) — canonical digest `a802c57fe34f8827…`,
  deterministic core `35d603fdfab533ad…`, 12 artifacts.
- `trust:verify --offline` — `valid: true`, digest `a802c57fe34f8827…`.
- `report:coverage --offline --verify-only` — `pass`, coverage digest `d0cc045b7da96a8c…`,
  machine artifact `bfba1cab…`, human document `24fc5234…`.
- `receipt:verify` — `valid: true`, 10 artifacts.
- `corpus:verify` (offline) — `pass`, 20 verticals, 15 source applications.
- `refusal-census --verify-only` — `matchesPublished: true`, **198 sites, unmoved**. No source
  changed, so no site moved; the census was verified rather than regenerated.

### 15.5 Did the screen's predictions hold?

**One of two, and the miss is the more useful half.** For `react-cra-redux-1a06509b` the screen
predicted "proven, or a witness reading" and the run returned proven at 9/9, count 0 — the
predicted install wall fell to exactly the policy the screen named. For
`react-your-spotify-1-5-0` the screen predicted witness and the run stopped one stage short at
build. The screen's *method* is not implicated: it derived predicted walls from the admission and
install rules at `ingest.ts:465-600` and `plan.ts:355-448`, and every one of those readings held
verbatim — the frontend root read as `client` without declaration, the CRA adapter claimed the
tree, install proceeded under `--allow-foreign-lockfile`. What the screen did not read, because

to the screen's method for the next batch: **read the seven era sources too**, because on this
lineage the era reading and the migration target can contradict each other, and that contradiction
is worth predicting rather than discovering at 15 s of install.
